rule: Lagna in Mesha (1st-house lord Mars, fire, movable; Mars also rules the 8th house)
text: With the Lagna in Mesha, Mars rules the 1st house and the chart is read from a movable fire sign. The rising sign describes the approach a person brings to new situations: here it tends to show up as directness, quick starts and a preference for acting before deliberating. Energy arrives in bursts and is spent openly. Mars also rules the 8th house for this Lagna, so the same drive is read for how endings and sudden change are handled. The reflective question is pacing rather than force.

rule: Lagna in Vrishabha (1st-house lord Venus, earth, fixed; Venus also rules the 6th house)
text: With the Lagna in Vrishabha, Venus rules the 1st house and the chart is read from a fixed earth sign. The rising sign tends to show up as a calm, deliberate manner, a liking for comfort and continuity, and a slow but firm way of deciding. First impressions are steady rather than striking. Venus also rules the 6th house here, so the same taste for ease is read against daily routines and the work that must be done regardless. The question is where steadiness becomes reluctance to move.

rule: Lagna in Mithuna (1st-house lord Mercury, air, dual; Mercury also rules the 4th house)
text: With the Lagna in Mithuna, Mercury rules the 1st house and the chart is read from a dual air sign. The rising sign tends to show up as a quick, conversational manner that meets new situations with questions, humour and more than one plan. Attention moves easily and may need a reason to stay. Mercury also rules the 4th house for this Lagna, linking the public face to home and inner settledness. It is read for how curiosity is given structure without being dulled.

rule: Lagna in Karka (1st-house lord Moon, water, movable)
text: With the Lagna in Karka, the Moon rules the 1st house and the chart is read from a movable water sign. The rising sign tends to show up as a responsive, protective manner that reads the room before speaking and remembers how people were treated. Moods colour the day more than for most Lagnas. Because the Moon moves fastest, the first house here is read closely with the Moon's own sign and nakshatra. The reflective question is how care is offered without taking on everyone's weather.

rule: Lagna in Simha (1st-house lord Sun, fire, fixed)
text: With the Lagna in Simha, the Sun rules the 1st house and the chart is read from a fixed fire sign. The rising sign tends to show up as a warm, self-assured manner that likes to be seen doing things properly and carries responsibility visibly. Pride and generosity sit close together. The Sun rules only this one house for the Simha Lagna, so its sign and dignity are read as the chart's centre of gravity. The question is how recognition is sought and how it is shared.

rule: Lagna in Kanya (1st-house lord Mercury, earth, dual; Mercury also rules the 10th house)
text: With the Lagna in Kanya, Mercury rules the 1st house and the chart is read from a dual earth sign. The rising sign tends to show up as a precise, observant manner, a habit of improving what is in front of it and a reluctance to claim more than can be shown. Modesty and exacting standards go together. Mercury also rules the 10th house here, so the public face and the career are read as one thread. The question is whether high standards serve the work or stall it.

rule: Lagna in Tula (1st-house lord Venus, air, movable; Venus also rules the 8th house)
text: With the Lagna in Tula, Venus rules the 1st house and the chart is read from a movable air sign. The rising sign tends to show up as a courteous, balancing manner that weighs the other side before answering and prefers agreement to victory. Charm is natural; decisiveness is learned. Venus also rules the 8th house for this Lagna, so the ease of the surface is read alongside what is kept private and shared. The reflective question is how fairness to others includes fairness to oneself.

rule: Lagna in Vrishchika (1st-house lord Mars, water, fixed; Mars also rules the 6th house)
text: With the Lagna in Vrishchika, Mars rules the 1st house and the chart is read from a fixed water sign. The rising sign tends to show up as a reserved, watchful manner that reveals little at first and commits fully once trust is given. Intensity is held rather than displayed. Mars also rules the 6th house for this Lagna, so this depth is read against daily effort, competition and the handling of obstacles. The question is how strong feeling is turned into steady purpose rather than held as pressure.

rule: Lagna in Dhanu (1st-house lord Jupiter, fire, dual; Jupiter also rules the 4th house)
text: With the Lagna in Dhanu, Jupiter rules the 1st house and the chart is read from a dual fire sign. The rising sign tends to show up as an open, principled manner that looks for the larger meaning in events and speaks its convictions readily. Optimism and bluntness often arrive together. Jupiter also rules the 4th house for this Lagna, tying the public outlook to home, learning and inner ground. It is read for how belief stays generous and open to other views.

rule: Lagna in Makara (1st-house lord Saturn, earth, movable; Saturn also rules the 2nd house)
text: With the Lagna in Makara, Saturn rules the 1st house and the chart is read from a movable earth sign. The rising sign tends to show up as a measured, practical manner that takes time to warm up and prefers results to promises. Responsibility is accepted early and carried quietly. Saturn also rules the 2nd house for this Lagna, so the same caution is read in matters of speech, family resources and what is kept in reserve. The question is how duty leaves room for ease.

rule: Lagna in Kumbha (1st-house lord Saturn, air, fixed; Saturn also rules the 12th house)
text: With the Lagna in Kumbha, Saturn rules the 1st house and the chart is read from a fixed air sign. The rising sign tends to show up as a detached, thoughtful manner that stands a little apart from the crowd while caring about the group as a whole. Ideas and principles come before personal display. Saturn also rules the 12th house for this Lagna, linking the public self to solitude, distant places and what is given away. It is read for how independence and belonging are reconciled.

rule: Lagna in Meena (1st-house lord Jupiter, water, dual; Jupiter also rules the 10th house)
text: With the Lagna in Meena, Jupiter rules the 1st house and the chart is read from a dual water sign. The rising sign tends to show up as a gentle, adaptable manner that absorbs the mood of its surroundings and prefers meaning and kindness to competition. Boundaries can be soft. Jupiter also rules the 10th house for this Lagna, so this receptive nature is read alongside the career and public role. The reflective question is how openness is kept without losing a clear centre of one's own.
